evidence: Hor. Ep. 2.2.215: tempus abīre tibi est
terms.comment: Abī! is “go away!”, or kindly “off you go”; abī intrō, “go inside”. With ab or ex and the place or person left, or with the supine of an errand (abī deambulātum, Ter. Haut. 587).

terms.gloss: go away, depart (from a place or a person)
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: “most frequently in all periods”, with ab or ex.

terms.gloss: away with you! (to a person or a thing)
terms.register: vōx cōmica: Plaut., Ter.; numquam apud Cic. (Lewis & Short)
evidence: Plaut. Amph. 580: apage tē ā mē (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Also “no thanks, away with it!”: apage, nōn placet mē (Plaut. Amph. 310, in Lewis & Short).
Traupman’s colloquial word; not found in Lewis & Short or the loci collections, so its quantities are Traupman’s.

phrases.latin: lūsistī satis, ēdistī satis atque bibistī; tempus abīre tibi est
phrases.english: you have played enough, eaten and drunk enough: it is time for you to go

phrases.latin: abī intrō, occlūde jānuam. jam ego hīc erō.
phrases.english: Go inside and shut the door. I’ll be back in a moment.
Shh! Be quiet and off you go.
